The capital of Australia is Canberra. It was chosen as a compromise between the two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne, which had been engaged in a rivalry for the national capital's location.

Following the Federation of Australia in 1901, there was significant debate over whether Sydney or Melbourne should serve as the seat of government. Sydney was the largest and most economically powerful city, while Melbourne was the cultural and financial hub. Neither city was willing to yield its status to the other. To resolve the impasse, the Australian Constitution mandated that the seat of government be located within the territory of New South Wales but at least 100 miles from Sydney. A heat pump moves more heat than the electricity it consumes because it transfers existing thermal energy from one location to another rather than generating heat through electrical resistance. This process relies on the thermodynamic principle that work can move heat against a temperature gradient, allowing the system to deliver multiple units of heat energy for every unit of electrical energy used to drive the compressor.
